title: dedicated-autoscaler: backpressure utilization reporting and SLO adjustments
author: Riya Patel
description: Motivation: Dedicated fleets sometimes experience transient backpressure during simultaneous burst traffic which is not reflected in existing utilization metrics and leads to missed SLOs. This PR adds a dedicated backpressure_utilization metric (per-fleet, per-priority) and improves utilization reporting to surface token-bucket saturation and queueing-related backpressure. Summary: emit a new histogram + gauge (backpressure_utilization, backpressure_bucket_fill) from the autoscaler runtime, wire metrics through the observability pipeline, add dashboards and SLO adjustments, and introduce a canary rollout flag. Design: metrics are emitted at decision points in pkg/autoscaler/controller.go and tokenbucket fill events in pkg/autoscaler/tokenbucket.go. The backpressure_utilization is computed as weighted_ratio(queue_time_over_threshold, tokens_requested, capacity_window) to reflect both queueing latency and token saturation. We add a smoothing window to avoid noisy spikes and tag metrics by fleet_id, priority, model_variant, and region. Dashboards: new dashboard file observability/dashboards/dedicated_autoscaler_backpressure.json and alert rule observability/alerts/backpressure-slo.yaml. SLO change: adjust Dedicated throughput SLO for burst windows from 99.9% to 99.7% for 60s burst windows while preserving long-tail 99.95% for steady-state 5m windows; this is gated by a config flag and rollout plan. Tests: unit tests added in tests/autoscaler/backpressure_test.go and pkg/autoscaler/metrics_test.go, integration test updated in ci/pipeline.yml to run an autoscaler stress scenario. Rollout: feature gate default=false; canary enables 10% fleets for 24h, then 50% for 48h, monitor backpressure_utilization and tokenbucket fill rate, then enable globally. Backwards compatibility: metric names are additive and opt-in via feature flag to avoid unexpected alert noise. Migration: dashboard/alert docs updated and SRE notified. Checklist: implemented metrics, dashboards, alerts, unit/integration tests, added docs, updated helm values.

merge_outcome: merged via squash-merge by Mei Chen after CI green and approvals (2/3). Release gated behind helm flag; no post-merge revert required.
release_notes: Add backpressure_utilization metric and dashboards; adjust Dedicated throughput SLOs for short burst windows; metrics off behind feature flag by default; SRE to run canary rollout as documented.
testing_and_rollout: Canary plan: enable feature flag for 10% of fleets for 24h, monitor backpressure_utilization and tokenbucket fill rate
If stable, expand to 50% for 48h then enable globally
Pre-merge: run ci/pipeline.yml autoscaler-stress job; post-merge: schedule SRE-runbook checks at +1h,+12h,+24h
Key metrics: backpressure_utilization (p95/p99), tokenbucket_fill_rate, queue_latency, request_success_rate
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: alert noise due to additive metrics. Mitigation: feature off by default; alerts scoped to canary fleets initially.
Risk: increased cardinality causing metrics cost. Mitigation: limited tag set and histogram buckets aligned with existing metrics cost model.
Risk: SLO relaxation miscommunicated to customers. Mitigation: SLO change documented in release notes and communicated to account teams; opt-in per-fleet via helm.
Risk: race in controller affecting token accounting. Mitigation: fixed race, added deterministic unit test and integration stress scenarios.
